symptom: The assistant stated that the user had assigned MOCATRIZ as the name of a manufacturing model even though the source corpus did not establish that user-authored naming decision.
root_cause: Assistant-generated interpretation was promoted to user-authored canonical intent without source-level attribution verification.
early_signals: The quoted wording used 'tú estás asignando' without a cited user-authored naming statement
The manufacturing meaning was introduced in assistant prose rather than established by explicit user authority
Cross-thread semantic reuse was accepted without provenance check
human_cost: Created a false canonical meaning and triggered a downstream token-collision diagnosis that was itself partly based on incorrect provenance.
prevention_rule: Never canonicalize a user preference, naming decision, policy, or semantic assignment unless it is explicitly user-authored or supported by durable authoritative evidence. Assistant-originated formulations must be labeled as proposals until adopted.
automated_detection: Canonical registry entries require an authority_source field distinguishing USER_AUTHORED, USER_APPROVED, or ASSISTANT_PROPOSED; ASSISTANT_PROPOSED entries cannot become canonical without explicit promotion.
